system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK — governing physical relation is electrical contact resistance and wear rate proportional to sliding speed, current density, and contact pressure. The wear rate (W) can be modeled as W = k × I² × v / (P × A), where k is material wear coefficient, I is current, v is surface velocity (188.5 m/s at 1800 rpm), P is contact pressure, and A is contact area. At 1.5 MW excitation (typical 300-500A DC), this creates measurable wear progression before thermal or vibration thresholds are reached.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — components: 1) plant historian data access API, 2) data processing software (Python/R with time-series libraries), 3) statistical analysis module. Materials: existing plant historian database. Instruments: standard plant DCS/SCADA system already collecting voltage, current, and excitation control signals. Procedure: extract 1-minute interval excitation current, voltage, and power factor data; calculate brush contact resistance from V/I ratio; track resistance trend using exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) with λ=0.1.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — implementation burden is light (software-only, no new hardware) compared to standard practice which relies on vibration/temperature monitoring. Operability is similar as it uses existing data streams. Maintenance is reduced as no new sensors required. Rough cost class is $5-10k in engineering time versus $20-50k for additional hardware monitoring systems. Worth it as it provides earlier warning without additional infrastructure.

EXECUTABLE TEST — protocol: extract 3 years of historical data from plant historian including excitation current, voltage, and resulting excitation transients. Apply the EWMA algorithm to calculate contact resistance trend. Instruments: standard data processing workstation with time-series analysis capabilities. Pass/fail threshold: predictor must trigger at least 14 days before all documented excitation transients with no more than 1 false alarm per year per machine. Duration: test against all available historical data (minimum 2 years). A test that fails to detect ≥90% of transients with ≥14 days warning or produces >1 false alarm/year kills the predictor.

DESIGN/INDICATOR: Exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) of brush contact resistance (V/I ratio) calculated from 1-minute historian data
THRESHOLD: 3-sigma increase in EWMA resistance trend above baseline (established during healthy operation)
TEST: As described above in EXECUTABLE TEST section
